title: Ezekiel Chapter 36 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 36 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 36 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 36.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 36, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Prophesy unto the mountains of Israel
Because the enemy hath said against you
Ye shall shoot forth your branches
I will multiply men upon you
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy unto the mountains of Israel
questions.explanation: This is the first command given in the chapter, specifically in Ezekiel 36:1.

questions.question: What does the Lord say the enemy has claimed about the mountains of Israel?
options: They are a possession of the heathen
They are to be tilled and sown
questions.correctAnswer: They are a possession of the heathen
questions.explanation: The verse states that the enemy has said, 'Aha, even the ancient high places are ours in possession' in Ezekiel 36:2.

questions.question: How have the mountains of Israel been affected according to Ezekiel 36:3?
options: They have been tilled and sown
questions.explanation: The verse states that they have been made desolate and swallowed up on every side in Ezekiel 36:3.

questions.question: To whom does the Lord speak in Ezekiel 36:4?
options: The mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys
questions.correctAnswer: The mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions that the Lord speaks to the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys in Ezekiel 36:4.

questions.question: What has the Lord spoken in against the residue of the heathen?
questions.explanation: The Lord states, 'I have spoken in my jealousy and in my fury' in Ezekiel 36:6.

questions.question: What will happen to the heathen around Israel according to Ezekiel 36:7?
questions.explanation: The verse declares that the heathen that are about Israel shall bear their shame in Ezekiel 36:7.

questions.question: What will the mountains of Israel do according to Ezekiel 36:8?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the mountains of Israel shall shoot forth their branches and yield fruit to the people of Israel in Ezekiel 36:8.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do for the mountains of Israel in Ezekiel 36:9?
questions.explanation: The Lord declares, 'For, behold, I am for you' in Ezekiel 36:9.

questions.question: What will happen to the cities according to Ezekiel 36:10?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the cities shall be inhabited and the wastes shall be builded in Ezekiel 36:10.

questions.question: What will the Lord do better than at the beginnings according to Ezekiel 36:11?
options: Multiply upon you man and beast
questions.correctAnswer: Multiply upon you man and beast
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to multiply upon Israel man and beast in Ezekiel 36:11.

questions.question: What will the people of Israel do according to Ezekiel 36:12?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the people of Israel shall possess the land and it shall be their inheritance in Ezekiel 36:12.

questions.question: The land of Israel is said to have devoured men according to Ezekiel 36:13?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the land is accused of devouring men and bereaving nations in Ezekiel 36:13.

questions.question: The Lord expresses joy for the possession of the land by the enemy according to Ezekiel 36:5?
questions.explanation: The Lord does not express joy; instead, He speaks against the heathen who have taken His land with joy and spite in Ezekiel 36:5.

questions.question: The mountains of Israel are said to be desolate in Ezekiel 36?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the mountains have been made desolate in Ezekiel 36:3.

questions.question: The Lord promises to forsake the land in Ezekiel 36:10?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises that the cities shall be inhabited and the land will be builded, not forsaken in Ezekiel 36:10.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 36 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 36 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will the Lord GOD not allow the land to do anymore?
questions.explanation: The Lord states in Ezekiel 36:14 that the land shall not devour men anymore, indicating a restoration of the land's purpose and a cessation of its previous destructive nature.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 36:15 promise will happen if the land does not cause men to hear the shame of the heathen?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:15 indicates that by not causing shame, the land will be free from reproach and will be restored to its intended state of blessing.

questions.question: What did the house of Israel do to defile their land?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:18 reveals that the Lord poured His fury upon them for the blood they had shed upon the land, indicating how their actions defiled it.

questions.question: What was the reason for the Lord scattering the house of Israel among the heathen?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:19 explains that the Lord judged the house of Israel according to their doings, which included idolatry and defilement of the land.

questions.question: What did the house of Israel profane among the heathen?
questions.explanation: According to Ezekiel 36:20-21, the house of Israel profaned the Lord’s holy name among the heathen, which is a serious transgression.

questions.question: Why will the Lord act for the sake of His holy name?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:22 clearly states that the Lord acts for His own name's sake, highlighting His commitment to His holiness and reputation.

questions.question: What will the Lord sprinkle upon the people to make them clean?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 36:25, the Lord promises to sprinkle clean water upon the people, symbolizing purification from their filthiness and idols.

questions.question: What kind of heart will the Lord give to His people?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26 states that the Lord will give His people a new heart and a new spirit, indicating transformation and renewal.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 36:24 promise regarding the gathering of the people?
options: They will be brought into their own land
They will live among the heathen
questions.correctAnswer: They will be brought into their own land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:24 promises that the Lord will gather His people from among the heathen and bring them into their own land, signifying restoration.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Lord sanctifying His great name?
options: It will bring honor to Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:23 indicates that the sanctification of the Lord’s great name will show the heathen that He is the LORD, revealing His character to all nations.

questions.question: The Lord's actions in Ezekiel 36 are primarily for whose sake?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:22 emphasizes that the Lord does not act for the sake of Israel, but for His holy name's sake, highlighting His sovereignty and integrity.

questions.question: The house of Israel's actions were likened to what in Ezekiel 36:17?
options: The uncleanness of a removed woman
questions.correctAnswer: The uncleanness of a removed woman
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:17 compares the house of Israel's defilement of the land to the uncleanness of a removed woman, illustrating the gravity of their sin.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will allow the heathen to continue to shame Israel.
questions.explanation: The Lord states in Ezekiel 36:15 that He will not allow the shame of the heathen to be heard in Israel anymore, indicating a future restoration.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord's fury was poured upon Israel for their idolatry.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:18 clearly states that the Lord poured His fury upon Israel for the blood they shed and for their idols, indicating His anger towards their idolatrous actions.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel are described as having a heart of stone.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26 mentions that the Lord will take away their stony heart and give them a heart of flesh, indicating a change in nature.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 36 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 36.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 36:27, what will God put within the people to cause them to walk in His statutes?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:27 states, 'And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes...'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 36:28, what is promised as the land given to dwell in?
options: The land given to your fathers
A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: The land given to your fathers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:28 says, 'And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be my people...'

questions.question: What does God promise to save the people from in Ezekiel 36:29?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:29 states, 'I will also save you from all your uncleannesses...'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 36:30, what will God multiply that will prevent reproach of famine among the heathen?
options: The fruit of the tree and the increase of the field
questions.correctAnswer: The fruit of the tree and the increase of the field
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:30 says, 'And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that ye shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen.'

questions.question: Ezekiel 36:31 speaks about the people remembering their evil ways. What will they do because of this remembrance?
options: Lothe themselves in their own sight
questions.correctAnswer: Lothe themselves in their own sight
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:31 states, 'Then shall ye remember your own evil ways... and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 36:32, why does God say He is doing these things for Israel?
options: For the sake of the prophets
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:32 states, 'Not for your sakes do I this, saith the Lord GOD...'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ruach' (רוח) in Ezekiel 36:27 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ruach' used in Ezekiel 36:27 is commonly translated as 'spirit' and refers to the divine spirit God puts within the people.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 36:34-35 where the land is described as becoming like the garden of Eden?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:35 uses a simile: 'This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden', comparing the restored land to Eden using 'like'.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God restoring the land and people as seen in Ezekiel 36:24?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:3 speaks of God’s everlasting love and restoration, echoing the gathering of Israel to their land in Ezekiel 36:24.

questions.question: Ezekiel 36:26-27 promises a new heart and spirit. Which New Testament passage fulfills this promise through the gift of the Holy Spirit?
questions.explanation: John 14:17 speaks of the Holy Spirit dwelling within believers, fulfilling Ezekiel 36:27’s promise to put His spirit within them.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the promise 'I will put my spirit within you' in Ezekiel 36:27?
options: I will give you a new heart
I will sprinkle clean water upon you
I will take you from among the heathen
I will gather you out of all countries
questions.correctAnswer: I will give you a new heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26 states, 'A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you,' immediately preceding verse 27.

questions.question: In the context of Ezekiel 36, what historical context explains the desolation and scattering of Israel referred to in verses 17-19?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:17-19 refers to Israel’s defilement of the land and scattering among the heathen, which historically aligns with the Babylonian exile.

questions.question: Which literary device is found in Ezekiel 36:37-38, describing the increase of men like a flock?
questions.explanation: The description of men increasing 'like a flock' in Ezekiel 36:38 is a metaphor comparing the people to a flock of sheep, symbolizing care and unity.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents the theological reason God gives in Ezekiel 36:32 for restoring Israel?
options: To fulfill the covenant with Abraham
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:32 and surrounding verses explain that God acts 'not for your sakes' but to sanctify His holy name among the nations.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 36:38, the waste cities will be filled with flocks of men as during Jerusalem’s solemn feasts.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:38 explicitly states that the waste cities shall be filled with flocks of men as during the solemn feasts of Jerusalem.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 36 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 36 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 36:8 teach about salvation?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:8 shows God's promise to restore His people, indicating His power to redeem and renew them.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 36:23 teach about God's glory?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:23 highlights that God acts for His own name's sake, emphasizing His ultimate purpose in glorifying Himself.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 36:26 teach about regeneration?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26 speaks of God giving a new heart, illustrating the doctrine of regeneration or new creation in Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 36:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:10 shows God's sovereignty in multiplying His people and restoring the land, reflecting His control over history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 36:29 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:29 illustrates God's faithfulness as He promises to save His people from their uncleannesses.

questions.question: How does this chapter connect to, prepare for, or fulfill a theme elsewhere in Scripture?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36 anticipates the New Covenant, where God promises transformation and His Spirit, as seen in Jeremiah 31:31-34.

questions.question: How does this chapter connect to the theme of judgment and restoration found in Isaiah?
questions.explanation: Similar to Isaiah's themes, Ezekiel 36 highlights God's restoration plan for Israel, ultimately fulfilled in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 22 and 32 teach about God's actions?
questions.explanation: Verses 22 and 32 emphasize that God acts not for Israel's sake but for His holiness, highlighting His grace and commitment to His name.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 25 and 27 teach about sanctification?
questions.explanation: Verses 25 and 27 show how God cleanses His people and places His Spirit within them, indicating a process of ongoing sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 11 and 36 teach about restoration?
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 36 highlight that God will restore both the people and the land, indicating a comprehensive restoration.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Ezekiel 36:16-20 shows that God abandons His people. What does Ezekiel 36:21-23 actually teach?
options: God's mercy is ultimately for His name's sake
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy is ultimately for His name's sake
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:21-23 reveals that God acts out of pity for His holy name, not merely for Israel's sake, demonstrating His commitment to mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 36:19 teach about human accountability?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:19 illustrates that God judged Israel based on their actions, highlighting human accountability for sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 36:15 teach about divine restoration?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:15 states that God will remove the shame of the heathen, indicating His intent to restore hope to His people after their despair.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 36:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:6 mentions God's jealousy, demonstrating His passionate commitment to His people and His holiness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 36:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:12 shows God's sovereignty in allowing His people to inherit the land, affirming His control over their destiny.
